title: Specific heat capacity of an aluminium block
stem: A student places a 12 V electric heater in a 1.00 kg aluminium block. The voltmeter reads 12.0 ± 0.1 V and the ammeter reads 4.0 ± 0.1 A. The temperature of the block is recorded every 120 s. The block is not insulated.

data.caption: Temperature of the block during heating

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage uncertainty in the power supplied by the heater.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the rate of temperature rise of the block.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the specific heat capacity of aluminium from these data.
markscheme: P = mc(ΔT/Δt) so c = P / (m × gradient)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The accepted value for aluminium is about 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. Explain why the experimental value is larger, and suggest one improvement.
markscheme: energy is lost to the surroundings / not all the heater’s energy heats the block
so the temperature rises more slowly than it should, making the calculated c too large (systematic error)
improvement: insulate the block (e.g. with foam/lagging) / use oil in the heater and thermometer holes for better thermal contact / start below room temperature and finish the same amount above it

title: Battery with internal resistance
stem: A battery of e.m.f. 9.0 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor and a 12.0 Ω resistor that are in parallel with each other.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the combined resistance of the external circuit is 3.0 Ω.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the current in the battery.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the power dissipated in the 12.0 Ω resistor.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The 12.0 Ω resistor is disconnected. Explain what happens to the terminal potential difference of the battery.
markscheme: so lost volts Ir decrease (to 1.0 V)
